correctness.rationale: For integer \(x\), the product \((x+j)(x+j+1)\) is nonnegative because its roots are consecutive integers, and for \(x\ge k\) the normalized quadratic is at least one. This proves the indicator majorization on the full lattice. Expectation gives the stated bound. The explicit three-point masses are nonnegative, sum to one, and match mean zero and variance \(v\); equality points of the majorant give uniqueness. The Cantelli-gap formula follows by exact algebra. A rational-arithmetic checker independently replays these identities.

value.rationale: Integer-valued laws are a natural probability class, and Cantelli is a canonical one-sided moment bound. The theorem exactly quantifies the lattice improvement for every variance and threshold, gives the complete extremizer, and exposes a reusable discrete dual-certificate mechanism. The improvement is structural rather than a numerical special case.
